title: Supported sections and flasque objects
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $s:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], and let $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be the complementary open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion]. Fix a finite commutative ring $\Lambda$ (in particular the finite ring $A_{E,n}$ fixed by [def-pur-conventions]). Work in the abelian categories of all sheaves of modules over the constant coefficient sheaves on the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules], with the identified coefficient inverse images [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. No constructibility condition is imposed on these sheaves. Write $j^*,s^{-1}$ for the underived module inverse images and $j_*,s_*$ for the underived direct images.

Let $\eta_{j,M}:M\to j_*j^*M$ be the unit of $j^*\dashv j_*$. Define the sheaf of sections supported on $Z$ by
$$
 \mathcal G_ZM=\ker(\eta_{j,M}).
$$
Explicitly, for an object $V\to X$ of the site,
$$
 (\mathcal G_ZM)(V)=\{m\in M(V):m|_{V\times_XU}=0\}.
$$
Its restriction maps are those of $M$. On a morphism $f:M\to N$, use the restriction of $f$ to these kernels; naturality of $\eta_j$ makes this a functor. Define
$$
 s^!M=s^{-1}\mathcal G_ZM,
$$
and on morphisms use $s^{-1}(\mathcal G_Zf)$. This is exactly the sheaf construction $s^!_0$ of [def-exc-proetale-sections-with-support]. The functors $\mathcal G_Z$ and $s^!$ are left exact. The notation $s^!$ denotes the closed inverse image of the supported kernel; it may coincide with ordinary restriction $s^{-1}$ for particular pairs, for example $Z=X$.

If $j$ is quasi-compact [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], the canonical unit of the closed inverse-image/direct-image adjunction gives a natural isomorphism
$$
 \mathcal G_ZM\xrightarrow{\sim}s_*s^!M.
$$
Thus in that case $\mathcal G_ZM$ is the closed direct image of the indicated sheaf on $Z$. For an arbitrary complementary open immersion this canonical comparison need not be an isomorphism, even with a nonzero finite coefficient ring and an affine base scheme.

A sheaf $I$ is called *flasque for this pair* if the unit $\eta_{j,I}:I\to j_*j^*I$ is an epimorphism in the abelian category of module sheaves, equivalently if its sheaf cokernel is zero. This is the pair-specific condition, with no assertion that the map on sections over every object is surjective.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-proetale-open-unit-evaluation] to the finite coefficient ring and the open immersion $j$. It identifies $(j_*j^*M)(V)$ with $M(V\times_XU)$ and the actual module-adjunction unit with restriction. Kernels in [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] are sectionwise, so their sections are exactly the displayed supported sections, with inherited restriction maps and module actions. Naturality $\eta_{j,N}f=(j_*j^*f)\eta_{j,M}$ makes $f$ carry each kernel into the next. These restrictions preserve identities and composition. Applying $s^{-1}$ gives exactly the object and morphism formulas of [def-exc-proetale-sections-with-support].

source.place: Tag 03DA, lemma-abelian; proetale.tex Tag 09BN, lemma-open-immersion; explicit kernel and naturality calculation

proof.text: On an object $W\to U$, the map $W\times_XU\to W$ is an isomorphism. The section formula in step 1 gives $(\mathcal G_ZM)(W)=\ker(\mathrm{id}_{M(W)})=0$. By the restriction identification in [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization] this says $j^*\mathcal G_ZM=0$. Assume now that the complementary open immersion $j$ is quasi-compact. The canonical-unit clause of [lem-exc-proetale-closed-essential-image] applies to this module sheaf, without a constructibility hypothesis, and gives $\mathcal G_ZM\xrightarrow{\sim}s_*s^{-1}\mathcal G_ZM=s_*s^!M$. This is the inverse of the identification written as $s_*s^!M=\mathcal G_ZM$ in the blueprint; equality is understood up to this specified natural isomorphism. This proves the positive comparison under the stated hypothesis. Steps 5–7 give an explicit counterexample to removing that hypothesis for all pairs; the correction is not inferred merely from the hypothesis of the cited theorem.

source.place: Tag 09AH, lemma-ses-associated-to-open; applying the existing canonical-unit theorem to the kernel

proof.text: For a left exact sequence $0\to M'\xrightarrow{a}M\xrightarrow{b}M''$, the sectionwise kernel description of [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] identifies $M'(V)$ with $\ker b_V$ for every object $V$. The restriction of $a_V$ to supported sections is injective. If $m\in(\mathcal G_ZM)(V)$ has $b_V(m)=0$, write $m=a_V(m')$ uniquely. Restricting to $V_U=V\times_XU$ gives $a_{V_U}(m'|_{V_U})=m|_{V_U}=0$; since $a_{V_U}$ is injective, $m'|_{V_U}=0$. Thus $m'$ is supported, proving $0\to\mathcal G_ZM'\to\mathcal G_ZM\to\mathcal G_ZM''$ left exact. The zero sheaf maps to zero by the same formula, and restriction of morphisms to the kernels gives $\mathcal G_Z(f+g)=\mathcal G_Zf+\mathcal G_Zg$, so this functor is additive. Apply the exact constant-coefficient inverse image $s^{-1}$ of [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact] to obtain left exactness of $s^!$. This argument does not require $j$ quasi-compact or surjectivity of any section map.

source.place: Tag 03DA, lemma-abelian (sectionwise kernels); Tag 04JC, lemma-flat-pullback-exact (inverse image); elementary kernel calculation

proof.text: The condition on $I$ is the stated definition: the cokernel of its open unit is zero in the abelian module-sheaf category [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. A sheaf cokernel is sheafified, so this condition does not identify epimorphy with surjectivity on every object. As edge checks, if $Z=\varnothing$ then $j=\mathrm{id}$ and $\mathcal G_Z=0$, while pair-flasqueness is automatic; if $Z=X$ then $U=\varnothing$, $\mathcal G_Z=\mathrm{id}$ and $s^!=s^{-1}=\mathrm{id}$, and pair-flasqueness is again automatic.

source.place: Tag 03DA, lemma-abelian; epimorphism criterion and the two identity/empty-complement calculations

proof.text: To test the unrestricted comparison, choose a field $k$ of characteristic $p$ and a nonzero finite commutative coefficient ring $\Lambda$ (for example $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_p$ and the allowed ring $A_{E,1}$ with $\ell\ne p$). Put $R=\prod_{n\ge1}k$, let $e_n$ be the coordinate idempotents, let $J=\bigoplus_{n\ge1}k$ be the ideal of finite-support sequences, and put $X=\operatorname{Spec}R$, $Z=\operatorname{Spec}(R/J)$ and $X_n=D(e_n)$. Since $e_nR=k$, $X_n\cong\operatorname{Spec}k$ is clopen. These opens are disjoint. A prime omitting $J$ omits some $e_n$, hence contains $1-e_n$, and is the coordinate prime for $n$. Thus $U=X\setminus Z=\bigcup_nX_n$. No finite subfamily covers $U$, so $j:U\to X$ is not quasi-compact, as $X$ is affine. There is no finite-type or constructibility hypothesis on the pair. For a pro-etale object $V\to X$, put $V_n=V\times_XX_n$ and $H_n(V)=\Lambda_{X_n}(V_n)$, the direct image along $X_n\hookrightarrow X$ of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Form the sectionwise product $P=\prod_nH_n$ using [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful]. Apply [lem-pur-module-sheaf-coproduct-local-support] to these sheaves on $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$: its $S\subset P$ is precisely the tuples that are finite-support on members of some covering, and is the coproduct $\bigoplus_nH_n$. Set $F=\operatorname{coker}(S\hookrightarrow P)$ in [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category].

source.place: Tags 03DA (lemma-abelian), 03DB (lemma-limits-colimits) and 03CO (lemma-limits-colimits-abelian-sheaves); agent counterexample to the unrestricted blueprint comparison: explicit affine pair and product/coproduct construction

proof.text: For this pair $s^{-1}H_n=0$. Indeed, in the inverse-image indexing formula of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image], replace any index $(V,\phi:W\to Z\times_XV)$ by $V'=V\times_X(X\setminus X_n)$. Since $Z$ is disjoint from $X_n$, $Z\times_XV'=Z\times_XV$, so $\phi$ factors through the new index. The arrow $V'\to V$ gives the restriction $H_n(V)\to H_n(V')=0$ in the opposite-index colimit. Every colimit generator therefore becomes zero, and its sheafification is zero. The identified-coefficient module inverse image has this same underlying abelian inverse image. The closed-immersion instance of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-immersion-limit-preservation] applies without a quasi-compact-complement hypothesis and gives $s^{-1}P=\prod_ns^{-1}H_n=0$; its coefficient-ring-isomorphism requirement is precisely the finite constant coefficient identification already in [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact]. Also $s^{-1}S=0$: by the adjunction of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], maps from $s^{-1}S$ to a sheaf $N$ are maps $S\to s_*N$, hence families of maps $H_n\to s_*N$, hence families of maps $s^{-1}H_n\to N$; this is a singleton for every $N$, so $s^{-1}S$ is the zero object. Exactness of [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact], applied to $S\to P\to F\to0$, yields $s^{-1}F=0$. On the localized site over $X_n$, every $H_m$ with $m\ne n$ is zero and $H_n$ is the constant rank-one module sheaf. For an object over $X_n$, every tuple in $P$ has at most the $n$th coordinate, so it already belongs to $S$; hence $S\to P$ restricts to the identity there. Exactness of the open inverse image, another instance of [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact], now gives $F|_{X_n}=0$. By [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization] open inverse image is this restriction. The opens $X_n$ cover $U$ in the pro-etale topology of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]: every affine open in the disjoint union $U$ meets only finitely many of them. The sheaf condition therefore gives $j^*F=0$.
